That means objects that were at the bottom become more visible (the bottom of the image now shows things that were previously below the frame). Conversely, the top of the image would show things that were above.

Let's define: camera moves up -> the image content moves down in the frame. So the top edge of the image now corresponds to a higher position in the world, showing more top? Hmm, I always get confused. Let's set coordinates.

World coordinate Y increases upward. Camera at height H, looking at scene. Image vertical coordinate v (0 at top, increasing down). A point in the world at height y projects to v proportional to (H - y) (higher world y -> smaller v, i.e., near top). If camera moves up by d, H' = H + d. Then v' proportional to (H + d - y) = (H - y) + d. So v' = v + k*d for some positive k (since larger (H-y) means lower in image, larger v). So image content shifts down by k*d. Yes: camera up -> content shifts down.
